cells.tense: You're holding it now, and it's holding you back — the standing is what you do, not what you're waiting for.
cells.place: at the moment before anything has chosen its shape
cells.ask: Offer the next bit of brightness — the thing you've been developing quietly — to someone who hasn't seen it yet, and let what you've built shine on its own account.
cells.core: You carry what's heavy without asking to put it down, and you don't perform the carrying. The strength is private and it's yours — found in what you hold, not what's handed to you. Nothing is decided yet about what this becomes, and the holding is already doing its work.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what's heavy and you don't need an audience for it.

cells.tense: You're bracing for a weight that hasn't landed yet — already gripping what no one has handed you.
cells.verb: forcing the hold before there's anything to hold
cells.place: in the middle of everything that hasn't happened yet
cells.ask: Let one thing be exchanged instead of carried alone — give something and receive something in the same motion, and let the exchange find its own level rather than forcing it.
cells.core: You're holding ahead of time. The difficulty hasn't arrived and you've already taken its shape, gripping against a future you can't write into. The endurance is real, but it's spending itself on loads no one handed you and nothing has asked you to carry.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping a weight that hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You were holding once, and you're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: waiting to be strong rather than already holding
cells.place: before anything has begun to become
cells.ask: Let one thing that's finished be seen as finished — name what it cost, let it be witnessed, and let completion be a release rather than a defeat.
cells.core: There's a strength that was yours and you've stopped drawing on it. Somewhere back there, the holding stopped working, so you stopped holding — and now everything that could be is still possible because nothing has been allowed to start. The capacity hasn't gone anywhere. The grip has.
cells.sheetLine: You have a strength you've stopped drawing on.

cells.tense: You're holding right now — the pen is in your hand — and you're talking as if the holding were just what's happening to you.
cells.verb: holding a strength you haven't claimed
cells.place: in the undecided middle of everything
cells.ask: Name one small thing you keep showing up for — not the big story, the ordinary refusal to quit — and say out loud that the persistence is yours; then let that hope have somewhere to go.
cells.core: You're already carrying it. The steadying, the not-quitting, the holding on when nothing looks different yet — it's running through you every day. But you describe it as just getting through, as if the strength were happening to you rather than being something you're doing. The strength is running. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already holding this. You just haven't said so.
